web_evidence.title: Full text of The good earth — Internet Archive/UCLA Library
web_evidence.note: The library scan of an authorized edition supplies the complete novel. Its opening, interior chapters, and ending consistently use nonparticipating third-person narration, chiefly following Wang Lung; first-person forms occur locally in speech or thought.

web_evidence.title: The Good Earth: Other Literary Devices
web_evidence.note: Explicitly identifies a detached third-person narrator and says the novel is written almost exclusively from Wang Lung's point of view.

web_evidence.title: The Good Earth Novel Units sample: Background Information
web_evidence.note: The teaching guide explicitly identifies the point of view as third-person omniscient and describes the continuous chapter 1–34 structure.

search_log: Searched "The Good Earth" "Pearl S. Buck" excerpt and first-chapter combinations; Google Books offered only limited-preview metadata, while Open Library led to a complete UCLA Library scan at Internet Archive.
Opened and sampled the Internet Archive full text at the opening, middle, late interior, and ending; all sampled sections sustained third-person narration.
Searched "The Good Earth" third person, narrator, and point of view; opened explicit descriptions from SparkNotes and the Novel Units teaching guide.

Searched the title with epistolary, diary, frame narrative, multiple narrators, and alternating point-of-view terms; found no credible evidence of a first-person frame or sustained change of grammatical person.
Checked the official Simon & Schuster page; it verified the work and overall story but supplied no narratorial excerpt or explicit POV description, so it was not used as person evidence.
person_note: The diagnostic quotes repeatedly show a nonparticipating narrator externally presenting Wang Lung and other characters while entering or summarizing their thoughts. The complete library text independently sustains that pattern from the opening through the ending, and explicit reference sources agree. Apparent first-person material in the quotes is dialogue, authorial paratext, or locally represented thought rather than an alternate base narrator. Sources differ over whether the third-person technique is limited, omniscient, or multiple, but that subtype disagreement does not affect the controlling THIRD label; no material uncertainty about grammatical person remains.
